clue.text: Mark on guitar appearing regularly in ferment

indicators.note: something that turns up at regular intervals shows only at every second step, so alternate letters are kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word

explanation.surface: A guitarist notices a stain on the instrument that keeps showing up in the fermenting brew.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the odd-numbered letters of 'ferment': F, R, E, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A fret is one of the raised metal ridges across a guitar's neck, marking where fingers press strings.

clue.text: Cold metal crushed by giant

indicators.note: something crushed is squeezed in the grip of another thing, so one piece sits inside the other

explanation.surface: A lump of chilly metal flattened under a giant's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' looks like a noun or a temperature reading, but it is the adjective for a sharp, piercing chill.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting wind is a sharply, painfully chilly one, so the adjective works as a synonym for very cold weather.

clue.text: End with little time in reserve

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside its letters

parts.note: a sub is a substitute, a reserve player
T is the abbreviation for time, 'little' signalling a short form

explanation.surface: Finishing with only a few minutes kept back.
explanation.walkthrough: T sits inside SUB, giving S-T-UB.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is the short remaining end of something, like a cigarette or pencil after use.

clue.text: Case where rule lifted, then allowed

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word raises its bottom letters to the top, so it reads upwards

explanation.surface: A legal case in which a ban was overturned and something then permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks legal but is a container for money; in a down clue 'lifted' turns the rule upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet is a small folding holder for cash and cards, a kind of pocket-sized case.

clue.text: Supply required outside, work on cold tap

indicators.note: a word required outside the others wraps around them

parts.note: a stock is a supply of goods

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A plumber notes the water supply needs a job done on the cold tap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work on cold' is read as one unit placed inside the supply; C for cold is the label found on taps.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopcock is a valve on a water pipe that shuts off flow, a kind of tap controlling the mains.

clue.text: Cheese spread clearly inspires Greek character

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece is drawn inside the other
spread out means scattered, so the letters are laid out in a new order

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A cheese spread that obviously motivates someone from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheese spread' reads as one thing, but 'spread' is the anagram signal; rearranged CLEARLY takes in PHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Caerphilly is a crumbly white cheese named after a town in South Wales, so it is an example.

clue.text: Toy in test I ran, failing

indicators.note: something failing is going wrong, so these letters fall out of their order

explanation.surface: A toy that broke down during a trial I conducted.
explanation.walkthrough: The eight letters of 'test I ran' rearrange to the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A train set is a model railway with track and locomotives, a classic children's plaything.

clue.text: Bone problem restricts bird

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A skeletal condition limits a bird's movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone problem' reads as one medical phrase; split it, so that 'Bone' is the definition and 'problem' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the flat breastbone in the middle of the chest, joined to the ribs.

clue.text: Wide of the mark describing flat object

parts.note: as, in the sense of 'describing him as a hero', means in the role or capacity of
a tray is a flat board for carrying things

explanation.surface: A description of a flat object that missed its target, like a thrown frisbee.
explanation.walkthrough: AS stands for 'describing' or 'in the role of'; TRAY follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Going astray means straying off course or missing the target, the same as being off target.

clue.text: Journey east by southern band

indicators.note: standing by something means being right next to it, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A musical group travelling east from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIP and E come after S. 'Band' suggests musicians but means a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow strip of colour, which is one sense of the word band.

clue.text: Position car alongside something round — roundabout!

indicators.note: alongside means next to, so the two pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: a ball is a round object
to park is to position a car

explanation.surface: A driving instruction: put the car next to the circular junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundabout' looks like a traffic circle, but it means approximate; the parked car comes second though it is clued first.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpark figure is a rough estimate, so ballpark as an adjective means approximate or roughly right.

clue.text: Old neon light flickering, one of a set

indicators.note: something flickering is unsteady and wavering, so these letters shift into a new order

parts.note: a tooth is one of a set of teeth

explanation.surface: An old neon sign flickering, part of a collection of lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of a set' sounds like another lamp, but it is a single tooth from a set of teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone ageing, from horses' gums receding with age so their teeth look longer.

clue.text: Crackers temporarily unavailable

definitions.meaning: first meaning: crazy, not all there
second meaning: away from one's desk for a midday meal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' suggests biscuits that have run out; it is the informal word for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for mad or eccentric, and literally a note saying someone has gone off to eat.

clue.text: Hook or snag?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to fasten or attach, as a trailer to a car
second meaning: a problem or temporary difficulty

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns about catching on something; one meaning is attaching, the other a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitch is to fasten one thing to another, and a hitch is an unexpected obstacle or setback.

clue.text: Stage where those such as hamsters do a backflip?

indicators.note: a backflip turns something head over heels backwards, so the letters run the other way

explanation.surface: A theatre stage where performing hamsters turn somersaults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' suggests a theatre, but it means a phase or step in a process.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is one stage in a sequence or process, as in taking things one step at a time.

clue.text: Killer parrot in a flap nips journalist

indicators.note: to nip is to pinch or grip, so one piece holds another
being in a flap is being flustered and agitated, so these letters are thrown about

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A flustered killer parrot pecks a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird is not the definition: it supplies letters, and the killer is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A predator is an animal that hunts and kills others for food, so a killer in nature.

clue.text: Game with striker in the box?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a stick struck to light a flame, kept in a small box

explanation.walkthrough: The football picture of a striker in the penalty box misleads; the striker is a little stick from a matchbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A football game is a contest between teams, and a small wooden stick you strike to make fire shares the word.

clue.text: Welcome, lie forgotten

parts.note: hi is a greeting of welcome
a story is a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: A greeting, and a fib conveniently let slip from memory.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is at the end: 'that's history' means over, done with, consigned to the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is history means it is over and gone, belonging to the past and no longer mattering.

clue.text: Vegetable stolen by crook, a leek

indicators.note: something stolen is held by the thief, so the letters are carried inside the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the next two

explanation.surface: A greens thief made off with produce from the allotment, a leek among it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read across 'croo-K, A LE-ek'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kale is a leafy green cabbage-family plant eaten as a vegetable, so it is an example.

clue.text: When everything seems to fail, yet nosh with seafood works

indicators.note: the works are machinery, so these letters are processed and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: On a bad day everything goes wrong, but food with seafood still succeeds; nosh is British slang for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' reads as a verb meaning succeeds; it is a noun-like signal that the fourteen letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a frustrating day when nothing goes right, matching a time when all efforts seem doomed.

clue.text: Fish caught by cook with little effort

indicators.note: something caught is trapped inside its captor, so one piece goes within the other

explanation.surface: A cook lands a fish without much trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a person, but it is the verb FRY, which holds EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something freely means doing it easily and without obstruction, needing little exertion.

clue.text: Stupid request almost entirely hollow

indicators.note: almost the entire word means all but the very end, so the final letter goes

explanation.surface: A daft request that is nearly totally empty of substance.
explanation.walkthrough: PLEA loses its last letter. 'Hollow' looks like an adjective about the request but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimple is a small dent or depression in the skin or a surface, a little hollow.

clue.text: Upset with bad tours in European capital

indicators.note: something that tours goes round and about, so these letters travel to new places

explanation.surface: A traveller annoyed with poor sightseeing trips in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' and 'bad' both look like anagram signals, but they are the fodder; 'tours' does the stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital city of Hungary, straddling the Danube, so it is an example.

clue.text: 2 Down open pie

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the answer to 2 Down, in its sense of sharp or acerbic
second meaning: a pastry case with no lid

explanation.walkthrough: 2 Down is BITING, read here as sharp or cutting, as in a biting remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart means sour or sharp in taste or tone, and a tart is a pastry with filling left uncovered.

clue.text: Dynamism about a type of German music

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

explanation.surface: Energetic Bavarian-style music full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: OOMPH wraps around A, which slots in before its final H.
explanation.definitionFit: Oompah is the rhythmic brass-band music associated with German beer halls, named for the tuba's sound.

clue.text: Bad lesson, every other one of those too

indicators.note: taking every other one of the preceding letters skips each alternate letter

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A poor lesson, and half of those were likewise poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' looks like an anagram signal, but it is part of the source: b-A-d-L-e-S-s-O-n.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too are synonyms, both meaning in addition or as well.

clue.text: Teach swimming group

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to train or educate
second meaning: a shoal of fish

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests swimming lessons; the swimming group is a large shoal of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to instruct them, and a school is a large group of fish moving together.

clue.text: Supporter of monarchy: lot I say about getting behind king

indicators.note: getting behind something means coming after it, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: about means in a different direction, so these letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A monarchist declares much of what they say is in support of the king.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of 'lot I say' are placed after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalist is a person who favours keeping a king or queen as head of state.
